 JUDGMENT

By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.

Shivakumar vs Gopal.V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
1 2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 08.05.2023 at about 8.30 am petitioner was going on his motor cycle bearing Regn No.KA-S-3901 on the left side of Bidadi-Mudavadi road, from Thorododdi village towards Heggadagere village slowly, carefully observing traffic rules and when the petitioner reached near Kadle factory, Heggadagere village, Bidadi, Ramanagara Taluk & Dist, at that time a Private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-16-A-5354 driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner came and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the impact, petitioner was thrown out from his motor cycle and suffered grievous injuries all over the body.
3. Immediately he was shifted to Bharath Kempanna hospital, Bidadi and admitted as inpatient on 08.05.2023.
That petitioner sustained bilateral hip arthritis (Secondary to AVN) left leg distal 1/3rd tibia fracture and other injuries.
He underwent CRIF with IMIL nailing to left tibia and other injuries were treated conservatively and advised to take follow up treatment.
That petitioner has spent Rs.1,25,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
That petitioner has to undergo few more corrective and implant removal operations.
(SCCH-12) 3 MVC. No.4071/2023 4. That due to the fracture petitioner is suffering permanent disability.
Petitioner was doing Electrician work and earning more than Rs.25,000/- per month.
That accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of private bus bearing reg.No. KA-16-A-5354.
The Bidadi Police have registered case against the driver of said private bus bearing No.KA-16-A- 5354 in Crime No.154/2023 U/Sec279,337 of IPC.
After investigation, police have filed charge sheet u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent R.C owner and 2nd respondent was insurer of private bus bearing No.KA-16-A-5354 and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
5. On issuance of notice, respondent No.1 owner of bus is served.
He remained absent before this court.
Hence, he is placed ex-parte.
6. 2nd respondent insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement denying the maintainability of case.
The manner of accident alleged by the petitioner is denied.
It is contended that petitioner was rash and negligent in riding the bike and he was solely negligent in the accident.
The nature of injuries, treatment taken, alleged medical expenses are denied.
The bus had no permit and that its driver had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

Age,
occupation, income and permanent disability alleged by the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds 2nd respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.
On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:-
ISSUES Shivakumar vs Gopal.

V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
2

1. Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in motor vehicle accident occurred on 08.05.2023 at about 8.30 am due to rash and negligent driving of driver of private bus bearing reg.no.KA-16-A-5354 when it hit his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-S-3901 while he was proceeding on Bidadi-Mudavadi road from Thoredoddi village towards Heggadagere village?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?

3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
8. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.12 documents are marked.

Dr.S.A.Somashekara Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital,
Bangalore got examined as P.W.2.
Through him Ex.P.13 and 14 documents are marked and closed their side evidence.
One Smt.Vidya.N, Motor Vehicle Inspector, Ramanagara got examined as R.W.1.
Through her Ex.R.1 to R8 documents are marked.
Smt .Sonia Thomas - Administrative Officer of 2nd respondent got examined as R.W.2.
Through her Ex.R.9 to 12. documents are marked and closed its side evidence.
9. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.

sentences.text:
On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and arguments of both sides, I answer the above issues in all the cases as follows: -
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3:
Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1 : Petitioner to prove actionable negligence on part of opponent bus driver filed chief examination affidavit and got examined as P.W.1.

In his chief examination he reiterated petition averments and relied upon FIR, first information, spot panchanama, IMV report, wound certificate,
final report and discharge summary.

Shivakumar vs Gopal.V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
3 13.
On perusal of those documents it can be seen that relative of the petitioner is 1st informant.

He gave first information to Bidadi police station on the date of accident and police have registered Crime No.154/2023 against the bus driver on the first information given by relative of petitioner by name Punith Raju M.
On the same day accident spot panchanama was drawn which shows the spot of accident is 22 ft wide tar road and the road is on north south direction.
Accident took place on western side 6 ft away from road edge.
Spot sketch is not (SCCH-12) 6 MVC. No.4071/2023 produced.
It is a junction in which 3 roads unite.
The time of accident is 8.30 Am.
As per the IMV report both the vehicles got damaged, there is front bumper damage to bus and several front left parts of the bike got damages.
The accident was not due to any mechanical defect as per the IMV report.
14. Barath Kempanna hospital has issued wound certificate in which it is mentioned history of RTA.
The nature of injury is shown as grievous.
In the charge sheet bus driver was found to be negligent and its owner is said to have not maintained the permit to the vehicle.
Hence both of them are charge sheeted for IPC and and IMV offences.
They have not questioned the final report.
Owner has not appeared before this court to contest the case.
15. 2nd respondent insurance company disputed the manner of accident.
In the cross examination of P.W.1, it is brought out that petitioner was on opposite direction in one way road.
His negligence in the accident is denied by him.

But his statement in cross examination dated 04.03.2025 reads as under:
"        . 
        .
      .  
     .    
    .      
 .

In the spot panchanam it is mentioned as 6 feet away on west side in the road of north south direction accident has taken place and as per cross examination of PW1 he was going towards Bidadi fater filling petrol.
Bidadi is on north side as per spot panchanama and it was junction.
Hence, there is some portion of negligence of petitioner in the accident.
Time of the accident being 8.30 Am both sides could have been observed to vehicles and accident could have been avoided if the proper caution was taken.
In that view of the matter this Tribunal is of the opinion that contribution of petitioner to the accident is 20% and contribution of the opponent bus driver is 80%.
Accordingly this issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.2 : To prove his age petitioner has produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.10 which shows his date of birth as 05.07.1986.

Accident took place on Shivakumar vs Gopal.V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
4 08.05.2023.
He was aged 37 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 36 years at the time of accident.
18. In respect of occupation it is stated that, he was an Electrician by profession and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
He has not produced any document to show his income.
Therefore notional income has to be considered.

Accident having taken place in the year 2023 the monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.16,000/-.
19.
In respect of permanent disability petitioner got examined Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2.
He is not a treated doctor.
He has assessed only disability.
According to him petitioner had sustained Bilateral hip arthritis (secondary to AVN ) + left leg (SCCH-12) 8 MVC. No.4071/2023 distal 3rd tibia fracture.
He underwent surgery and fracture is minimally mal-united with implants in situ.

In his evidence he has mentioned that on examination of petitioner on 08.05.2023 for assessment of disability petitioner complaints of pain and difficulty in walking, climbing stars,
squat, sit cross leg, and inability work.
There is wasting and shortening of left lower limb is seen by the doctor.
On examination he found that petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting and shortening of left lower limb and surgical scars are seen.
The P.W.2 doctor has assessed the permanent physical disability of left lower limb @42% and whole body disability @ 21%.

Petitioner being electrician, the injury may come in the way of his occupation and in these circumstances, in the opinion of this court the functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is 20%.
Accordingly this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of private bus bearing No.KA-16-A-5354.

Hence,
petitioner is entitled to compensation.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced 15 medical bills at Ex.P.12.
He has paid amount of Rs.79,926/- towards medical expenses.
Those bills are disputed but no concrete evidence is laid to dispute the bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.79,926/- under this head.
(ii) Food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges:
The petitioner underwent surgery to left tibia as per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.11.
It shows that petitioner was (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.4071/2023 admitted to Bharath Kempanna health Care unit, Bidadi from 08.05.2023 to 13.05.2023.

entities.text: Bharath Kempanna health Care unit, Bidadi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Total 6 days.
Considering the cost of living, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges in 2023, Rs.15,000/- is awarded under this head.
(iii) Loss of income during laid up period: Minimum 3 months is required to recover from grevious injury.

Hence, his loss of income during laid up period is considered as Rs.16,000 X 3 months Shivakumar vs Gopal.V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
5 Rs.48,000/-.
(iv) Loss of future income due to Disability : As per the findings given above, there is 20% functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is Rs.16,000/- income X 12 months X 20% disability X 15 multiplier to the age group of 36-40 years which comes up to Rs.5,76,000/- compensation is awarded under this head.
(v) For Future medical expenses:
As per the evidence of doctor there is need for future surgery for removal of implants but, no estimation is provided to that effect.
Hence amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded for future medical treatment.
(vi) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained fracture.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- .
(vii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life : There is evidence of doctor to show that grievous injury has affected the normal life of the petitioner.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.60,000/- is awarded under this head.

 conveyance charges.

iii Loss of income during laid up period 48,000/-
iv. Loss of future income due to 5,76,000/-
 disability v. Future medical expenses 25,000/-

vii Physical discomfort and loss of 60,000/-

Contributory negligence on part of (-)1,72,785/-
 petitioner at @20%
 Grand total 6,91,141/-
21.
Liability:
RW2, authorized representative of the insurance company is examined and contend that there was no valid permit the vehicle as on the date of accident.
But RW1 RTO of Ramanagar is examined and he has produced the permit details which are renewed covering the date of accident.
Hence insurance company is liable for the portion of negligence on part of the bus driver.
There is valid insurance to the opponent vehicle as on the date of accident Hence, 2nd respondent insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to petitioner.
As per the settled law, interest @ 6% from the date of petition till the date of deposit will have to be awarded.

Shivakumar vs Gopal.V on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172935812/
6
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
 (SCCH-12) 11 MVC. No.4071/2023  ORDER  The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs. 6,91,141/-
with interest @ 6% pa on Rs.6,66,141/-
from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).

Respondent No.2 being insurer of bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within 60 days from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation amount without making FD.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
